The '''Jacobian matrix''' assembles all first [[partial derivative]]s of a [[map function]] between two [[vector space]]s.

== Formal definition ==

Let $V \subset \mathbb{F}^n, W \subset \mathbb{F}^m$ be [[vector space]]s.

Define $f:V \to W$

$$
\forall \vec x= (x_1,\dots,x_n) \in V:
f(\vec x)=\bigl(f_1(x_1,\dots,x_n),\dots,f_m(x_1,\dots,x_n)\bigr).
$$

If all first partial derivatives of $f_i$ exist at point $\vec x$, the '''Jacobian matrix''' of $f$ at $\vec x$

$$
\mathbf{J}_f(\vec x)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_1}(\vec x) & \cdots & \dfrac{\partial f_1}{\partial x_n}(\vec x)\\[8pt]
\vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\[8pt]
\dfrac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_1}(\vec x) & \cdots & \dfrac{\partial f_m}{\partial x_n}(\vec x)
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

== Properties ==

The gradient of $f_i$

$$
\nabla f_i(\vec x)= (\text{row}_i)^T
$$
